subject: general
question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6% per annum rate of interest for the period from 20 February 2024 to 21 April 2024.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total days from 20 Feb to 21 Apr in a leap year = 9 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 21 (Apr) = 61 days.

Time in years (leap year) = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year.

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

SI = (4000 × 6 × 1/6) ÷ 100 = 4000 ÷ 100 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 6% p.a.

Time period = 20 February 2024 to 21 April 2024

 

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 Simple Interest Timeline P = ₹4000 | R = 6% p.a. | Leap Year (366 days) 
• 
• 20 Feb 
• 29 Feb 
• 31 Mar 
• 21 Apr 9 days 31 days 21 days 
 Total = 61 days = 1/6 year 

**Calculations:**

⇒ The year 2024 is exactly divisible by 4, making it a leap year. So, February has 29 days.

⇒ Number of days counted in February = 29 − 20 = 9 days.

⇒ Number of days counted in March = 31 days.

⇒ Number of days counted in April = 21 days.

⇒ Total days (T) = 9 + 31 + 21 = 61 days.

⇒ Since it is a leap year, total days in the year = 366 days.

⇒ Time converted to years (T) = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year.

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6 × (1 ÷ 6)) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (4000 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 4000 ÷ 100 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leap Year Rule

A year is a leap year if it is perfectly divisible by 4. Century years are leap years only if divisible by 400. Leap years have 366 days, with 29 days in February.

Counting Days for Interest

By standard banking convention, the day of deposit is generally excluded, but the day of withdrawal is included when calculating the total number of interest-bearing days.

Total Amount Formula

The total amount at the end of the time period is the sum of the initial Principal and the accumulated Simple Interest. Formula: A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].
